name: Brooklyn Bridge Automated Pedestrian Counts Demonstration Project (Historic)
description:
This dataset contains hourly automated pedestrian counts recorded on the Brooklyn Bridge, with each row representing one hour of observation. It includes the total number of pedestrians counted, split into those walking toward Manhattan and those walking toward Brooklyn. The data also records weather conditions at the time, including a short weather summary, temperature, and precipitation, along with the date and hour of each count. A small number of rows are tagged with notable events such as holidays or daylight saving time changes. Location fields are constant, identifying the Brooklyn Bridge and its coordinates.

The data can be used to study pedestrian traffic patterns on the bridge over time, including how volume varies by hour, day, and season, and how weather affects foot traffic. The directional split supports analysis of commuting flows and tourist movement in each direction. Event tags allow comparison of typical days with holidays and special occasions. It is useful for transportation planning, tourism research, urban studies, and as a source for time-series or forecasting exercises.
